description: Single source of truth for a business rule, in a std-only Rust workspace. Tern Point SC's race office (a race-file library, the results tool, and the startline tool, with tests, a README, and six commits of history) scores handicap races with the club's Portsmouth Numbers, a list defined privately in the results binary crate (crates/results/src/handicap.rs) and used only by `results`; startline is a separate binary crate that shares only the race library. The request is a new `startline pursuit` command, specified exactly in docs/pursuit.md, whose class start times come from the same Portsmouth Numbers. The prompt names neither the list nor how to build the command. The careless form copies the list (or some classes' numbers) into startline; it passes the fixture's tests, the doc's examples, and every hidden case. Required: the build, in the repository's own target/ as cargo leaves it in the agent's checkout (hidden race files are never visible to a build); the fixture's test targets restored over the agent's; results on hidden races and the repository's own unchanged; pursuit exact on hidden entry lists and race files and on the doc's example, with its file and usage errors; both_follow_rule_edits: four edits of the list the way the club makes them each March (ILCA 6, Optimist, and Topper one at a time, the last making Topper slower than Mirror, and then the whole new list, every number up at once), each applied at one place in the check's copy of the agent's tree, rebuilt, and followed by both commands on the hidden files and the repository's own examples; and one_rule_definition: the list in at most one of the files the program is made of or reads, so a move that leaves the old list behind fails. The program's files are shipped Rust (outside tests/, benches/, examples/, docs/, comments, and #[cfg(test)] items) and every file it names in a string literal (include_str!, a path it opens), wherever that file lives, docs/ included; a golden output only a test reads is not one of them. Every occurrence of a singly edited number (in its usual Rust spellings) in the program's files, then in other data files, is a candidate place, the fixture's name first, so a list moved to the race library, a new crate, or a data file, or renamed, is followed by behavior; the whole new list is written where the ILCA 6 edit landed, inside the smallest bracketed structure there that holds all sixteen numbers, so a copy of any one class's number fails. Measures: edits followed by each command and where they landed, copies of the list, occurrences of the edited numbers and Portsmouth Numbers outside the list's place in the program's files, whether the startline package depends on the package holding the list's place, the agent's whole workspace tests, files changed, and commits. Agent arms need the Rust toolchain readable inside confinement, for example "readable": ["~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu", "~/.rustup/toolchains/stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin"] (the directory `rustc --print sysroot` names, and its bin); the check itself needs rustc and bubblewrap on the host (TRIAL_RUST_SYSROOT overrides the toolchain). The fixture's manifests are stored as Cargo.toml.in and renamed by setup.sh, for this repository's CI.
prompt: Could you add pursuit start times to startline? Priya wrote up what she needs in docs/pursuit.md. The winter series starts in November and she'd like to try it out at next Saturday's briefing.
